title: Telemetry sandbox cutover checklist + Prom/Grafana QoS & TF module notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a working checklist and notes file for doing a controlled cutover of telemetry in private deployments (VPC / on-prem sandboxes -> staging). Focus is on Prometheus + Grafana + OTEL collector + log shipping. The intent: validate Terraform modules, perform a canary upgrade of the collector, confirm remote_write and log egress, and verify QoS/retention settings before prod cutover.

Scope / Assumptions:
- Target environment: customer-managed VPC staging cluster (k8s 1.27) with dedicated telemetry namespace (telemetry-ops).
- Existing telemetry consists of older OTEL Collector (v0.70), Prometheus (2.44), and a mix of fluent-bit agents for logs.
- We will test: 1) TF module instantiation & state migration, 2) OTEL upgrade to distribution v0.77 with prom receiver, 3) Prom remote_write to Cortex/Thanos-compatible endpoint, 4) Grafana provisioning via JSONnet / provisioning folder, 5) S3-backed log archive and lifecycle.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: contains shell smoke tests, quick config snippets, and rollback knobs.

High-level plan (stages):
1) Local validation & dry-run TF (CI sandbox)
2) Deploy to isolated telemetry sandbox (single node canaries)
3) OTEL collector canary upgrade + smoke tests (metrics + traces + logs)
4) Prometheus config rollout (scrape relabels + remote_write)
5) Grafana dashboards/alerts provisioning validation
6) Full cutover, monitoring, and rollback window

Pre-cutover checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm TF remote state bucket exists and team has access (bucket: redwood-telemetry-states-staging)
- [ ] Branch + PR for TF changes and run terraform plan in CI sandbox (GH PR linked above)
- [ ] Snapshot current Prometheus TSDB on staging node (create snapshot via /api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot)
- [ ] Export current Grafana provisioning directory (for backup)
- [ ] Ensure all alert receivers have test endpoints (pagerduty/ops slack test channel)
- [ ] Create k8s namespace telemetry-ops-sandbox and resource quota: cpu=2, memory=8Gi to bound canary impact

Terraform module notes / gotchas:
- Module layout: modules/telemetry/collector, modules/telemetry/prometheus, modules/telemetry/grafana-provisioning, modules/telemetry/log-shipper
- State migration: we have a legacy monolith tfstate; split plan: create new statefile for prometheus module, import resources by k8s resource id, and ensure resource names match new module naming conventions (prefix: rdw-telemetry-{{env}}).
- Variables to watch: prom_retention (default 15d), prom_remote_write_enabled (bool), collector_image_tag (string), log_shipper_backend (s3|splunk|elasticsearch).
- Recommended default values for staging: prom_retention=7d, scrape_interval=15s (adjust by scrape group), remote_write_rate_limit: 2500r/s.
- TF provider versions: pin kubernetes provider to ~> 3.0 and helm provider to 2.x to avoid drift with cluster (k8s 1.27).
- CI step: terraform plan should run with TF_VAR_force_diff_check=true to block accidental retention changes.

OTEL collector upgrade plan (canary-first):
- Target: move from collector v0.70 -> v0.77 (Redwood distribution).
- Canary approach: deploy collector-canary (1 replica, smaller resources) in telemetry-ops-sandbox with identical config except: write_to file_exporter (local) and metrics scrape frequency = 10s for smoke tests.
- Steps:
  1) Apply collector chart (helm + values file) in canary namespace.
  2) Confirm collector registers in service discovery and begins receiving metrics from sidecars (check /metrics endpoint).
  3) Run smoke scripts (see below) to ensure metric ingestion and trace export.
  4) If OK for 30m, roll collector to 2 replicas and gradually increase traffic by adjusting service selectors to include collector-canary.
- Rollback knob: helm rollback to previous release; TF change is purely additive until switch is made to new image tag.

Prometheus configuration notes:
- Scrape config examples to include relabeling telemetry-ops pods with job="rdw-app"
- Use pod/service annotations where possible to avoid hardcoding scrape targets.
- Add relabeling block (example):
  - source_labels: ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app"]
    action: replace
    target_label: job

- remote_write: use a write-relay with credential injection from k8s secrets. Example remote_write snippet (yaml):
  remote_write:
    - url: https://cortex-staging.redwood.net/api/prom/push
      bearer_token_file: /etc/secrets/cortex/token
      queue_config:
        max_shards: 8
        min_shards: 1
        capacity: 2500
      write_relabel_configs:
        - source_labels: [__name__]
          regex: ".*_internal_.*"
          action: drop

- QoS/Retention: for staging run 7d retention and tune compaction: storage.tsdb.retention.size: 50GB per replica as a cap.
- TSDB backup: enable Prometheus snapshot cronjob before any config change.

Grafana provisioning / dashboards:
- Use provisioning provisioning/dashboards/*.json and datasource YAML for the staging grafana instance. Keep dashboards in repo: infra/grafana/provisioning/staging.
- Alert rules should be validated with grafana-toolkit / grafana-cli dry-run.
- Example checklist:
  - [ ] Add datasource with secure secret from k8s secret (grafana-ds-cortex)
  - [ ] Deploy dashboards (dashboard ids tracked in repo) and open test panel
  - [ ] Validate alert evaluation in sandbox (set evaluation interval to 30s in sandbox to accelerate validation)

Log shipping design notes:
- Options considered: fluent-bit -> s3 / fluentd -> s3 / otel-collector logging pipeline -> s3 + CDN. We recommend migrating toward OTEL collector for unified telemetry unless customer has heavy custom filters in fluentd.
- Staging config: otel-collector logs receiver -> batch exporter -> s3 using S3 exporter (multipart upload), set lifecycle on bucket: 90d -> archive to Glacier after 180d.
- Ensure IAM/minimum perms principle: putObject, multipartUpload, listMultipartUploadParts, putBucketLifecycle.
- Backpressure handling: configure processor/k8sattributes and queue_settings; set max_batch_size=4096, timeout=10s.

Smoke tests (commands to run):
- Metrics smoke: curl http://collector-canary.telemetry-ops-sandbox.svc.cluster.local:8888/metrics | grep rdw_app_request_count
- Prom remote_write check: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --data-binary @sample-metrics.prom https://cortex-staging.redwood.net/api/prom/push -v and expect 200
- Grafana panel: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GF_TOKEN" https://grafana-staging.rdw.local/api/annotations | jq '.'
- Logs: kubectl logs -n telemetry-ops-sandbox deployment/otel-collector-canary | tail -n 200 | grep "exporter/s3"

Validation & observability during cutover:
- Metrics: check per-route token-level latency spike charts, prometheus scrape success rate, and remote_write queue length.
- Traces: verify trace ids propagated across services in 10 sample requests using a sampler that injects X-Trace-Id header.
- Logs: confirm TTL on archived bucket and test retrieval of a sample object from S3 lifecycle.
- Alerting: mute non-critical alerts for 1 hour during cutover; keep P1 alerting active.

Rollback plan (if things go wrong):
- Collector issues: helm rollback collector deployment and re-run smoke tests; if stateful data missing, point remote_write back to previous endpoint.
- Prometheus misconfig: revert TF change by applying previous module state, restore prometheus config from snapshot, and restart Prometheus with previous config.
- Grafana regressions: restore dashboard provisioning folder from backup and redeploy.

Post-cutover checks (first 72 hours):
- Confirm scrape error rate <0.1%
- Remote_write retry queue stable and no sustained backpressure (>5min at >75% queue utilization)
- Alerts firing as expected (runbook link check, escalate if not)
- Cost check: estimate token/ingest delta from baseline and report to finance weekly during trial window.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide final retention policy for prod (15d vs 30d) — finance to sign-off (PD-2047)
- Confirm if customer wants OTEL-only log pipeline or mixed fluentd migration (action: ping solutions-eng)
- Add test harness that synthesizes 5k/s metrics for stress testing remote_write in sandbox (todo: small python generator in infra/tools)

Next immediate steps (this doc's TODOs):
- [ ] Create GH PR with TF split plan (owner: Maya) -> GH: redwood-infra/telemetry-terraform#412
- [ ] Provision telemetry-ops-sandbox namespace and minimal quota (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Prepare canary values.yaml for otel-collector (owner: Jia)
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour cutover window with SRE and Solutions (owner: Maya)

Notes to self / friction points observed in prior cutovers:
- Watch for serviceAccount token TTL causing sudden 401s on remote_write (need k8s projected tokens or long lived secret)
- Prometheus remote_write failures often correlate with misconfigured TLS CA in upstream; include ca_bundle in secret and test with curl from inside cluster.
- Grafana provisioning can silently fail if folder perms wrong — check grafana logs for "file not found" during startup.

References:
- GH PR: redwood-infra/telemetry-terraform#412
- Jira: PD-2047 (telemetry retention review)
- Slack thread: #private-deployments-telemetry (link pinned in GH PR)

End of doc (working draft).

-- Maya
